facts.text: Brampton recorded $1.58 billion in industrial, commercial and institutional construction value in 2025, including $997 million in industrial development.
Advanced manufacturing is Brampton's largest employment sector and accounts for almost a quarter of the city's workforce.
Magna International employs more than 2,000 people across eight facilities in Brampton.
Brampton is home to CN's intermodal terminal, the largest intermodal railway terminal in Canada, and to Canada's largest inland port.

overview: Brampton grew 10.6 percent between 2016 and 2021 to reach 656,480 residents, the fastest growth among Canada's largest municipalities. With a median age of 36.0 and a median household income of $111,000 in 2020, the city combines a young population with above-average earning power.

Its 182,472 occupied private dwellings sit on 265.89 square kilometres, so density is high and neighbourhoods are compact. For a local business, that means a steady stream of new households forming and moving in, many of them young families who have not yet chosen their regular providers and who search online first.
